title: Breathed in dust or smoke
scenario: Coughing, throat and chest irritation after breathing dust from a collapsed building or nearby smoke.
steps: Move to fresh air away from the dust or smoke.
Rinse your mouth and nose with clean water; sip water to ease the throat.
Loosen tight clothing and rest — sit upright rather than lying flat.
Cover your nose and mouth with a mask or damp cloth if you must be near dust again.
Call 911 for trouble breathing, wheezing, chest pain, or bluish lips — especially in people with asthma, heart, or lung conditions.
If coughing or irritation persists past a day, seek medical care.
do_not: Do not return to a heavy-dust area without protection.
Do not ignore worsening shortness of breath.
